featured_reviews.name: Atul Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Nestled deep within the narrow, quaint lanes of Bandra (a classic single-car road experience!), Tatsu offers a charming and distinct spot for dessert lovers. Its small corner location makes finding it an adventure, adding to the allure of this specialty bakehouse.

The Baked Tart Experience

Tatsu specializes in baked Japanese Cheesecake Tarts, offering a textural experience that is truly distinct from traditional cheesecake. The tarts are firm yet creamy, a unique balance that requires a flavor pairing to match one's exact preference.

I sampled three varieties:

The Lemon Mousse Cheesecake Tart was the clear winner, earning an easy 4 out of 5. The tangy lemon mousse cut through the richness of the baked base perfectly.

The Apple Crumble Cheesecake Tart scored a respectable 3.5 out of 5. The crumble topping added a nice textural contrast, and the apple filling was comforting.

The Blueberry Cheesecake Tart was good but didn't quite hit the high notes of the others, coming in at 3 out of 5. While the flavor was pleasant, it was the least distinctive of the trio.

Overall Verdict

Tatsu is a must-visit for anyone looking for a unique dessert experience in Mumbai. You need to explore their menu to find the perfect flavor balance for your palate. The baked texture is their signature, setting them apart from standard patisseries.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A1 Bakery in Bandra is one of those super old-school spots tucked away in a tiny nook — no seating, just a small counter where you can grab your food and maybe stand around while you eat. We landed up here after Googling “old bakeries in Bandra,” and A1 popped up in almost every article, so naturally, we had pretty high expectations.

But honestly? It was quite underwhelming.

We tried a bunch of things — their veg and non-veg patties (both decent), the quiche (again, decent), and the very hyped-up chicken lollipops, which were… just okay. Nothing was outright bad, but nothing really wowed us either.

That said, the prices are quite reasonable. So for the price, the food is fair. But the overall experience? Meh. Definitely not something I’d go out of my way to recommend. I think the hype kind of worked against it — we walked in expecting a “hidden gem” kind of vibe and left feeling like it was all just very average.

If you’re nearby and want a quick, no-fuss bite, sure, give it a shot. But don’t expect anything iconic.

featured_reviews.name: Rohan Kini
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently stumbled upon this old-school bakery on Hill Road, located conveniently near Bandstand.

They offer a wide range of items, from puffs, croissants, and patties to cakes and muffins. While the vegetarian options are a bit limited compared to the meat selection, the taste is excellent and very fair for the price.
Note:These are budget-friendly snacks, so don't expect chunks of chicken in every bite, but the flavor is definitely there!
Also don't go by their display , if tray is empty on display they still may have it stored inside .

The staff is friendly and the service is incredibly quick. They bake in batches about three times a day, so if your choice isn't piping hot, just ask them to heat it up for you—they are happy to oblige.

Be prepared to queue up, especially on weekends and in the evenings. Even with a crowd, the line moves fast, so don't let the rush pull you away.

Pro Tip (Safety First!):
Try not to wait too long on the footpath outside. Cause once Salman Khan made a very "impactful" appearance right there with his car... and we all know how that story goes....😂😂

featured_reviews.review_text:

The chicken puff was just okay. The chicken croissant was great. The cinnamon bun was very nice - not too sweet.
Everything was nice and bite -sized. Service was quick and thoughtful. Not particularly interactive. There's standing place right there, a bit shielded from the road by shrubs and bushes. Nothing to sit on.

featured_reviews.name: Crystal Sequeira
featured_reviews.review_text:
A-1 used to be something else until a few years ago in terms of the taste and quality of their food. Even though the prices of all the window items have seen a steady increase, the quality has if anything worsened to a point of question.

I recently ordered food and spat almost all of it out in utter disgust! Chicken cutlets - no sign of chicken, huge and deceiving packed with filler (maida, cornflour, maybe a dash of potato) with an overpowering taste of cinnamon. Absolutely sickening to be duped this way. Chicken pan rolls, one of their best selling items, had sharp bones in it which could get masked under the crunch of the coating if not chewed carefully. Not to forget the horrid chunks if chewy chicken fat/ maybe the wastes of chicken on second thoughts, interspersed through this seemingly tasty roll. One word - GROSS! Mutton puffs were a saving grace, though dripping in oil, were fairly edible with some sign of meat. Non vegetarians, ditch this place. Vegetarians - if you’re a fan of cornflour and maida filler, this place is a go to!

Never ever eating from this place again!

featured_reviews.review_text:
This is my 2nd time ordering from Tharu Sweets. Although I live in Dubai, I had someone who got the mithai for me all the way from Mumbai. The quality of their mithai is topnotch 👌🏽 I've been looking for a mithai place that makes sweets in authentic asli cow ghee since over 10 years now 😅 since I'm quite a foodie with a sweet tooth, but until I taste the motichoor laddoo from Tharu, every other place has been a disappointment. Tharu mithai is the real deal, you can literally taste the ghee and all the mithai is fresh and tastes delish. I've ordered a variety of their sweets- motichoor laddoo, kesar katli, besan laddoo, sohan halwa, mahn ka laddoo and some others that I liked the description of but I forget their names 😂
My only issue is that their online ordering is a bit slow and won't accept international debit cards or even the Indian Bank cards. I had to use my aunt's Indian Bank account to do an online direct transfer.
Final thoughts, I definitely recommend this place for good quality mithai and pricing is reasonable.

featured_reviews.name: Jianna Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Its always been a favorite amongst my family. They have the best of Pure Ghee Sweets.. around here. Its gotten even better since a few years now. They have airconditioned their shop... and their level of hygeine has gone up tremendously too. Sweet and Savoury... all their goodies are great.. but do note that.. the prices are steep too.
The Dal Pakhwan is to die for.. seriously scrumptious..!!
And then their Alu Tikki and chholey is yum too.
Been there since so many years now... but this was the first time that I tasted.. and then bought Mysuru Paak. Its simply the melt in the mouth variant. I have tried it at so many South Indian and Maharashtrian sweet shops... but this is by far the best I've had till date.

Must mention Motichoor Laddoo too. After having the laddoo from regular local mishtaan bhandars here... I had started to hate it.
But Tharu's laddoo.. took me back in time.. straight to the halwai shops at Chowk in Allahabad.. now.. Prayagraj. Fried in Pure ghee and steeped in syrup.. yet one can feel each boondi coming apart in every bite. Rarely does one come across.. such perfectly made laddoos nowadays. Well Tharu's motichoor ladoo.. was almost there. Real Motichoor..!!
You must try.. if you havent already.

Must keep something for my next review. So adieu folks. More after my next visit there..

I carried two boxes of sweets all the way from Mumbai to the USA with so much excitement, telling my family I brought special sweets from India. To my surprise, when I opened the boxes, the sweets were completely dried out—clearly old stock.

This isn’t about the money; it’s about the effort, excitement, and sentiment behind bringing these sweets home. I am extremely disappointed and do not recommend Chandu Halwai to anyone. Please don’t waste your money here.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Aher
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bombay Sweet Shop – A Modern Take on Traditional Indian Sweets

Bombay Sweet Shop beautifully reimagines Indian mithai with a contemporary twist, both in presentation and flavours. The packaging is premium and festive, making it an excellent choice for gifting—especially during Diwali or special occasions. What stands out is the innovation: classic sweets are thoughtfully reinvented with modern textures, balanced sweetness, and high-quality ingredients.

The variety is impressive, ranging from fusion mithai boxes to snackable treats like barks and savoury options. Each item feels well-crafted and fresh, with consistent quality across products. The store itself is vibrant and inviting, and the staff is helpful when it comes to explaining the concept and recommending combinations.

Pricing is on the higher side compared to traditional sweet shops, but the creativity, hygiene, and overall experience justify it. If you’re looking for something unique that still respects Indian flavours, Bombay Sweet Shop is definitely worth a visit—great for self-indulgence and even better for premium gifting.
